title: Using the stack
description:
The tests check that every function leaves `rbx`, `rbp` and `r12` to `r15` as it found them. These functions **must** use `rbx` and `r12` (or other callee-saved registers) for their work, so save them with `push` and restore them with `pop`:

| Function | Result |
|---|---|
| `sum_of_squares(a, b, c)` | a² + b² + c², keeping a running total in **rbx** |
| `reverse_string(s)` | reverses the string in place by pushing every character and popping them back |
| `largest_gap(array, n)` | the largest difference between two neighbours, `array[i+1] - array[i]`, for n >= 2; keep the best so far in **r12** |

starter.solution.asm:
sum_of_squares:
        xor     ebx, ebx
        mov     rax, rdi
        imul    rax, rdi
        add     rbx, rax
        mov     rax, rbx
        ret

reverse_string:
        ret

largest_gap:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
sum_of_squares:
        push    rbx
        xor     ebx, ebx
        mov     rax, rdi
        imul    rax, rdi
        add     rbx, rax
        mov     rax, rsi
        imul    rax, rsi
        add     rbx, rax
        mov     rax, rdx
        imul    rax, rdx
        add     rbx, rax
        mov     rax, rbx
        pop     rbx
        ret

reverse_string:
        xor     ecx, ecx
.push:  movzx   eax, byte [rdi + rcx]
        test    al, al
        jz      .pop_all
        push    rax
        inc     rcx
        jmp     .push
.pop_all:
        xor     edx, edx
.pop:   cmp     rdx, rcx
        jae     .done
        pop     rax
        mov     [rdi + rdx], al
        inc     rdx
        jmp     .pop
.done:  ret

largest_gap:
        push    r12
        mov     r12, [rdi + 8]
        sub     r12, [rdi]              ; the first gap
        mov     ecx, 1
.loop:  lea     rdx, [rcx + 1]
        cmp     rdx, rsi
        jae     .done
        mov     rax, [rdi + rdx*8]
        sub     rax, [rdi + rcx*8]
        cmp     rax, r12
        cmovg   r12, rax
        inc     rcx
        jmp     .loop
.done:  mov     rax, r12
        pop     r12
        ret

hints: `push rbx` (and `push r12`) at the start, `pop` in the reverse order before every `ret`. Then you may use them freely.
For `reverse_string`, push each character (as a 64-bit register) while walking to the terminator, then walk again from the start and pop them back into place.
rules: Save rbx with push in sum_of_squares.
Save r12 with push in largest_gap.
Pop the characters back in reverse_string.
unitTests:
test "sum of squares"
    sum_of_squares(1, 2, 3) == 14
    sum_of_squares(-4, 0, 5) == 41
    sum_of_squares(1000, 1000, 1000) == 3000000
test "reversing with the stack"
    reverse_string(@"stressed") => "desserts"
    reverse_string(@"ab") => "ba"
    reverse_string(@"x") => "x"
    reverse_string(@"") => ""
test "the largest gap"
    largest_gap([1, 4, 6, 15, 16], 5) == 9
    largest_gap([10, 3], 2) == -7
    largest_gap([5, 5, 5], 3) == 0
